label: George Knapp
narrative: Knapp converted forty years of Nevada-desert sourcing into sworn congressional testimony on 9 September 2025, and in doing so put the contractor-custody allegation into the Congressional Record under his own name. Testifying before the House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, he told the panel that Robert Bigelow and a colleague from the AAWSAP program 'met with and negotiated with senior executives at Lockheed Martin and hammered out a deal wherein Bigelow's company, BAASS, would receive a quantity of unusual material that had been stashed away and protected at a facility in California,' adding flatly: 'That material was not made here.' Asked directly by Rep. Tim Burchett which corporations hold the material, Knapp answered 'one of them is Lockheed,' declined to treat the company as villainous - 'they are doing what they were asked to do' - and offered the committee a list. Pressed by Rep. Nick Begich to name individual gatekeepers, he named Dr. James Ryder at Lockheed and, separately, Glenn Gaffney of CIA. He also placed on the record his interviews with Alfred O'Donnell, first general manager of EG&G in Nevada, and with Senators Harry Reid and Howard Cannon. Knapp's 1989 Bob Lazar reporting, which he re-affirmed in the same testimony, is the origin point of the modern S-4 reverse-engineering narrative. He is not a cleared insider and does not claim to be; his value is that he is a named journalist who has now sworn to his sourcing before Congress, converting decades of tier-3 anecdote into tier-2 record.
